One oil step thicker (e.g. 500 → 550 cSt), both fronts identical, keeping the front/rear oil offset. Silicone shock oil thins as it heats, so a hot track leaves the baseline under-damped — bouncy, packs less, bottoms on landings; thicker restores the intended damping. Thicken for the MAIN event's temperature, not a hot qualifier: if it cools by the final, over-thick oil goes wooden and loses grip.
sources: JQRacing — THE Guide (Joern Neumann, 1/8 buggy), Set-up Advice: hot weather calls for thicker shock oil
RC Car Stars — The Effects of Temperature on Silicone Shock Oil (~50 cSt / 2.5wt per 10° change)
EuroRC — Basic Shock Oil Setup (silicone oil thins in heat)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One oil step thinner (e.g. 500 → 450 cSt), both fronts identical, keeping the front/rear offset — roughly ~50 cSt per 10° below your baseline temp. Silicone shock oil thickens as it cools, so a cold track leaves the baseline over-damped — harsh, low grip, slow to take a set; thinner restores the intended damping and mechanical grip in the cold.
sources: RC Car Stars — The Effects of Temperature on Silicone Shock Oil (cold thickens silicone; run lighter, ~50 cSt / 2.5wt per 10°)
The RC Racer — Racing on Low Grip / cold conditions: softer, thinner shock oil
EuroRC — Basic Shock Oil Setup (temperature ↔ viscosity)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One oil step thinner on the rear (e.g. 450 → 400 cSt). Same cold-thickening mechanism as the front; thinner rear restores forward bite and compliance lost to over-damping in the cold.
sources: RC Car Stars — The Effects of Temperature on Silicone Shock Oil (cold thickens silicone)
HUDY Off-Road Set-Up Book p.26 §1.9.1 — softer rear shock oil = more rear traction / compliance
EuroRC — Basic Shock Oil Setup (temperature ↔ viscosity)

engine_scope_refusal.refusal: Engine tuning (needles, plugs, mixture, temperatures) is out of my scope for now — getting it wrong can destroy an engine, so I only advise on chassis settings I have verified rules for. Refer to your engine manufacturer's manual for factory needle baselines, and tune from rich to lean in small steps with a temp gauge.

1-8-tt-buggy.notes: Section ids mirror packages/schema cars.ts COMMON_SECTIONS / NITRO_SECTIONS / BRUSHLESS_SECTIONS exactly - schema owns the section-id and ChassisRegistryEntry SHAPES; the class-facet VALUES are canonical HERE and in kb/chassis/registry.json (category=offroad, scale=1/8, type=buggy; exported as FACET_* constants from packages/kb/src/index.ts). The example facet values in schema cars.ts comments and its test fixture (buggy / offroad-competition) are placeholders, not vocabulary - sectionApplies matches raw strings and fails closed, so author section conditions against THIS vocabulary only. A chassis template's own category field (e.g. 1-8-nitro-buggy in inferno-mp11.json) is the chassis/<cat>/ extraction-directory name, a different fact, never a class facet. A car's visible sheet = common + sections for its power_type (sheetSections); class-facet conditions fail closed when labels are unknown. Chassis belonging to this class are listed in kb/chassis/registry.json with category/scale/type matching this file's facets.
